rule: Umbrella criterion 4's second half, mechanised by scripts/sole_home_scan.py. Every row excuses one (source, value) pair: a 'coincidence' says the integer is not that shape count at all, a 'forced_restatement' says it is and that R-17, R-19 or R-34 made writing it unavoidable. Since the umbrella's Amendment H of 2026-08-14 the forced rows are criterion 4's ruled CARVE-OUT rather than its open residue: a leaf's own adjudicating receipt may state that leaf's value, on three conditions -- the restatement sits inside an artifact adjudicating that exact leaf, names the leaf by its path, and agrees with the committed receipt or declares what it supersedes. This file is what keeps the carve-out from widening: every row is one site, a row that outlives its site fails, and a site with no row fails.
how_a_row_retires: A forced row retires when its site stops stating a count of a COMMITTED baseline -- because a re-capture superseded the figure, or because the artifact stops adjudicating that leaf. Editing the sources is not available and never was: a superseded oracle receipt is never edited (R-15/R-18 amendment) and a commit body is history. What changed on 2026-08-14 is the reading, not the mechanism: Amendment H rules these sites carved out rather than owed, and the scan's job became holding the carve-out to its three conditions instead of counting a debt.  The deferral-coverage capture of 2026-08-15 did it a fourth time and at the widest reach yet, because it moved every coupled census at once -- both entry counts, both leaf counts and the coupled numeric-leaf count -- so every row still keyed to one of them stopped having a site in the same commit: two commit bodies' R-34 lines, one oracle receipt's numeric-leaf figure, one allowlist's leaf figure now two captures old, and the three coincidences whose integers stopped colliding with a live count the moment the count moved. None is re-keyed and none is edited -- a commit body is history, a superseded oracle receipt is never edited, and an allowlist two captures behind states a figure no reader should be sent to. The residue that remains is the one row whose figure no capture since has superseded. It rose again the same day, by three rows across three sources, when the RW-scenarios oracle pass filed verdicts on three of the counters that capture moved: an oracle receipt states the two values of the leaf it adjudicates (R-19), and when the leaf IS a shape counter there is no way to pose the verdict without writing the figure. That is the carve-out working rather than widening -- each of the three sits inside the artifact adjudicating its own leaf, names it by its path, and agrees with the committed sole home -- and it is exactly the rise the pinned residue exists to make visible.  The amp-armed capture of 2026-08-15 did it a fifth time and at the same reach, because it too moved every coupled census at once: the four rows still keyed to the deferral capture's figures -- that capture's own allowlist row, and the three RW-scenarios verdicts on the counters it moved -- stopped having a site together, and none is re-keyed or edited. In their place the same two shapes the mechanism predicts: one forced restatement, this capture's allowlist claiming the coupled leaf counter in order to supersede the claim before it, and the campaign's first coincidence row, an event ordinal in an older allowlist that became visible the moment coupled_golden.entries moved onto the same small integer. A coincidence row is not a carve-out: it says the integer is not that figure at all.  The window-armed capture of 2026-08-16 did it a sixth time and at the same reach, because it too moved every coupled census at once: the two rows keyed to the amp-armed capture's figures stopped having a site together -- that capture's own allowlist row, and the campaign's first coincidence row, an event ordinal that had become visible only while coupled_golden.entries sat on the same small integer and stopped being a site the moment the counter moved off it. Neither is re-keyed and neither is edited. One arrived in their place, the shape the mechanism predicts: this capture's allowlist claiming the coupled leaf counter in order to supersede the claim before it. So the forced count is unchanged at two across two sources while both of its members are new-or-standing rather than carried, and the coincidence count falls to zero -- which is what a coincidence row is supposed to do, since it never said the integer was the figure.  It rose again the same day, by three rows across three sources, when the RW-window-scenarios oracle pass filed verdicts on three of the counters that capture moved -- the same shape and the same cause as the rise the deferral capture's own oracle pass produced, one capture earlier: an oracle receipt states the two values of the leaf it adjudicates (R-19), and when the leaf IS a shape counter there is no way to pose the verdict without writing the figure. Each of the three meets Amendment H's three conditions -- it sits inside the artifact adjudicating that exact leaf, names the leaf by its path, and agrees with the committed sole home (54683, 18027 and 19 respectively) -- so what the count records is that three more artifacts now adjudicate a counter, not that the carve-out widened. The fourth counter this capture moved, /metadata/scenario_count, also drew a verdict and is not a site: it is not a /metadata/fingerprint/ leaf, so no shape context puts its integer in the scan's reach. That is the detection rule holding its stated jurisdiction rather than an omission.  The swing-term capture of 2026-08-16 did it a seventh time and at the same reach, because it too moved every coupled census at once: the four rows keyed to the window-armed capture's figures stopped having a site together -- that capture's own allowlist row, and the three RW-window-scenarios verdicts on the counters it moved -- and none is re-keyed or edited. In their place the same two shapes the mechanism predicts, both of them for the second time: one forced restatement, this capture's allowlist claiming the coupled leaf counter in order to supersede the claim before it, and one coincidence, a leaf-delta in the Phase 4 boundary capture's own R-34 line of cause that became visible the moment coupled_golden.entries moved onto the same small integer. So the forced count falls to two across two sources and the coincidence count rises from zero to one -- and the coincidence is the one to read twice, because it is the second time an entry counter landing on a small integer has lit up a sentence that was never about a fingerprint. A count of members will keep passing through the small integers, so a coincidence row on the entry counters is a recurring event and not an anomaly.  And it rose to four, across four sources, the same day, when the RW-swing-scenarios oracle pass filed verdicts on two of the counters that capture moved. This is the third run of the pattern the paragraph above names -- a capture moves every coupled census, the rows keyed to the previous figures retire together, and then the oracle pass on that capture's own leaves raises the count by one row per counter it adjudicates -- and the rise is smaller than the last one because the pass itself was smaller: three verdicts rather than six, one per qualifying occurrence the capture's own allowlist declared, and only two of the three adjudicate a leaf that IS a shape counter. Each of the two meets Amendment H's three conditions against the figure this capture made live: the restatement sits inside the artifact adjudicating that exact leaf, names the leaf by its path, and agrees with the committed sole home. The third verdict, on /coupled_scenarios/swing_term_armed_carry_roster, is not a row and could not be: a scenario membership is not a count, so it states no figure for the scan to see.

allowances.reason: Not a shape count. The Phase 4 boundary capture's R-34 line of cause counts leaves added to cleaver_bloodsong_roster -- '+20 for the ten Expose Weakness support_damage_multiplier containers the authority move adds' -- and that integer became visible to the scan only when coupled_golden.entries moved onto it. The sentence is about ten containers of two leaves each and about no fingerprint at all.

R-17: an allowlist states the expected old and new value of every path it claims, and this allowlist claims /metadata/fingerprint/leaves in order to supersede the swing-term coverage claim on it, so it cannot make the claim without stating the figure. It agrees with the committed sole home, docs/receipts/campaign-fingerprints.json, as the full-coverage re-capture made it live.
R-19: an oracle receipt carries the two values of the leaf it adjudicates, and this leaf IS a fingerprint shape counter, so the receipt cannot state the question without stating the figure

a_superseded_count_stops_being_a_site: The charge-price PIN re-capture did it a fourth time, and for the first time in the pair jurisdiction: it is the only capture since the 0B boundary to move golden.leaves and golden.numeric_leaves, so the two rows that stated those two superseded figures -- 1483b46e's, the 0B capture commit's own line of cause under R-34, and oracle-0A.2-golden-leaf0.json's numeric-leaf figure under R-19 -- retired outright, with no re-keying available to either: a commit body is history and a superseded oracle receipt is never edited. The 0A.2 receipt keeps its entry-count row, which that capture did not move. The scan reads the LIVE counts from campaign-fingerprints.json, so a receipt restating a count a later re-capture superseded stops being a site the moment the capture lands -- which is what the criterion says, since it binds a count OF A COMMITTED BASELINE and a superseded figure is no longer one. The campaign-close coupled re-capture moved coupled_golden.leaves and retired six rows that way; the seventh, this file's H2 allowlist, is re-keyed to the new value because an allowlist states both sides of the move it claims. The stale-row check is what makes that visible rather than quiet: a row outliving its site fails. The 2026-08-14 exact-capture move did it again and in both directions: three rows stating the old exact leaf count retired the moment the capture superseded it, and one allowlist's unrelated occurrence count became a collision the same day. Both are recorded rather than reasoned about, which is what the stale-row check is for. The campaign-close BOUNDARY re-capture did it a third time: the H2 allowlist's row retired outright because its stated figure is now two captures old, and the dispositions allowlist's row was re-keyed to the figure that capture made live -- the same two moves, in the same order, for the same reason. The full-coverage re-capture did it again, in the same two directions: the swing-term allowlist's row retired because the figure it states is a capture old, and this capture's own allowlist arrived claiming the same counter in order to supersede the claim before it. The retirement landed one commit ahead of the arrival, which is why the scan reported the arriving site rather than nothing at all.
why_rows_leave: An allowance excuses a receipt or commit body for restating a live golden shape count. When the baselines are re-captured the figure moves, the restatement stops naming a live count, and the row stops excusing anything: it is removed rather than carried, which is what the scan's stale check is for. The receipts themselves keep their numbers — they record what was true when they were written.
